findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - on Windows, a close on an existing pull request waits for the code's CI while another checkout upgrades.
After review, `close.py:442` can wait in `checks.let_finish` before pushing review records. That wait does not create the CI run-start record that this scan needs (`checks.py:138,165-175,247-262`), so upgrade leaves the close alive and attempts to replace its environment. The install can still fail even if upgrade was started separately through uvx. Also, a normal `forge upgrade` started from the installed tool keeps its own environment in use while invoking the installer. The [documented Windows limitation](https://github.github.com/spec-kit/upgrade.html) applies to both active environment users.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a Windows user upgrades the installed Forge while a close waits for CI.
The fake installer checks only `closing.pid` and then writes a separate launcher; both commands are started with the test interpreter (`tests/test_lanes_agents.py:97-102`), so it cannot detect the upgrade process holding the installed environment open. The fixture also starts without an existing pull request (`tests/test_close.py:235-239,292`), bypassing the unrecorded pre-push CI wait described above. This test can therefore pass while those Windows upgrade cases remain broken.
